title: Antagonist Split - Gabriel V2
author: Andre Assunção
desc: Arms and shoulders development, coupled with a focus on isolation for the lats and chest.

ex.note: Warm up for quad work
Do one warmup set before starting to go heavy. Go deep focus on quad. This should be done in the 45 degree linear machine, not the "pendulum" one.
Control the weight, milk the stretch. Don't bounce on the bottom of the move.
Do this not on the machine, but the free weight version. Hold a plate and go all the way down.
Put the back seat as far back as possible, so you can lay back. Adjust the pins to maximize stretch, control the weight.
Lean forward, maximum stretch. Focus on increasing the weights, this move will be important.
In the machine where you elevate the knees too.

ex.n: Lying Behind The Back Neck Plate Elevation
ex.note: Careful with the weight, use about 2.5/5kg to start
Focus on chest activation, wide grip should help here. Project your chest upwards, arching the back. Your elbows should go as deep as possible, go slowly for chest activation.
Use the hammer strength machine, the plate-loaded one where you can do the movement seated with flared elbows.
Arnold style, control the stretch.
Warm up with one set before going heavy, should not hurt triceps if well executed.
Extremely important movement, lay perpendicular to the bench resting only the upper back on it. Should be a tremendous stretch on the lats.
Extremely important for brachialis, take this seriously

ss.note: You should get a rope and alternate between overhead and pushdown. Do both of them partial, not reaching 90. On the pushdown, focus on the contraction, use a lighter weight.
On the overhead part, focus on maintaining the the upper arm as stable and fixed as possible. It is going to reduce the weight, but keep the arm stable. Should reduce tricep pain.

ex.note: Full range lateral raise
Best forearm exercise. Seat on a bench, rest one arm at a time on the inside of your leg. Let the dumbbell roll to your fingers then curl it back, minimum momentum involved. Will burn.
Do it focusing on the triceps, especially contracting them. Don't let the elbows flex more than 90, but go as deep as comfortably possible.
Use the fancy machine they have there, control the weight throughout the movement.

On the overhead part, focus on maintaining the the upper arm as stable and fixed as possible. It is going to reduce the weight, but keep the arm stable. Should reduce tricep pain.

ex.note: Full range lateral raise
Best forearm exercise. Seat on a bench, rest one arm at a time on the inside of your leg. Let the dumbbell roll to your fingers then curl it back, minimum momentum involved. Will burn.
Do it focusing on the triceps, especially contracting them. Don't let the elbows flex more than 90, but go as deep as comfortably possible.
Use the fancy machine they have there, control the weight throughout the movement.
